sections.title: Conditional probability and two-way tables: choose the reference group

blocks.setup: Two-way table slice: 25 students commute; 10 commuters cycle (40 students total). Find the percentage of commuters who cycle.

steps.label: Reference group
steps.text: Commuters: 25 students. The question asks for the share among this group.

blocks.takeaway: The denominator is the reference group (commuters), not the full class of 40. In a table, divide a cell by its row total for a row percentage or its column total for a column percentage; percentages sum to 100% within that row or column.

blocks.text: P(A | B): among B, share also in A = count(A and B) / count(B). Order matters; P(A | B) and P(B | A) usually differ. Assume equal case weights and a non-empty reference group.
Report every proportion as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place and name the reference group (e.g., 40.0% of commuters).
Split cases by a categorical variable; compute one summary (such as a mean or count) per group.
Output: one row per non-empty group, not one row per original case. Compare groups using the same summary: mean with mean, count with count.
